newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate ends higher after choppy trade.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate ends higher after choppy trade.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate closed higher after a choppy session as short-term rates were supported by expectations of the money market tightening after Bank Negara's intervention in the foreign exchange market, dealers said.
It traded mostly between 7.0 and 8.0 percent before a late surge to 8.5 percent, they said.

"Today's rise in short-term rates is mainly due to Bank Negara's intervention in the forex market," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank. But he said the rise appeared to be overdone and rates could fall back slightly on Friday.
Dealers said many finance companies were caught short and were bidding up rates.
The central bank could have sold between $700 million and $1 billion on Wednesday to stem the slide of the ringgit, foreign exchange dealers said.
Earlier, one-, two- and three-week money were traded at 8.0/8.5 percent, up from between 6.80 and 7.20 percent on Wednesday.
One-month money was done at 7.55 percent and three- and six-month at 7.60 percent, against 7.30/45 percent previously.
Dealers said any tightening would be temporary due to maturity of a 900-million ringgit long-term government bond issue on Thursday and a 500-million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue on Friday.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange fell across the board in anticipation of rising interest rates, futures dealers said.
At 0900 GMT, the benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was down three points to 92.63, or an implied yield of 7.37 percent.
September and December fell five each to 92.62 and 92.61, or 7.38 and 7.39 percent respectively.
